hero.headline: Construction worker killed by vehicle in I-95 work zone south of Tradition
hero.teaser: A 45-year-old dump truck driver was killed after being hit by another construction vehicle inside a work zone on I-95 just south of Tradition on Monday night, according to the Flor
hero.body:
A 45-year-old dump truck driver was killed after being hit by another construction vehicle inside a work zone on I-95 just south of Tradition on Monday night, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The driver stepped out of their dump truck on the northbound lanes and was struck by a tractor with a sweeper traveling south, repaving the area as part of an improvement project.

The construction worker was transported to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, where they later died. The driver of the other truck was arrested on an unrelated warrant, FHP said.

The incident occurred during an improvement project on I-95 in Port St. Lucie. Workers were actively repaving the area when the fatal collision took place. The agency has not released the names of those involved in the crash.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
cards.body:
Paige O'Donnell, 62, was arrested Monday after Martin County deputies executed a search warrant at her home on Alligator Street in Palm City and discovered 36 Border Collies living in severe neglect. O'Donnell faces 72 criminal charges: one felony animal torture charge and one misdemeanor confinement charge for each dog. Her bond was set at $270,000, and a judge ordered her not to possess any animals if released.

Deputies found the dogs covered in feces and urine inside a home where the air conditioning was not working and floors were covered in waste and garbage. Sheriff John Budensiek said some of the normally black-and-white Border Collies were so covered in feces they appeared nearly solid black. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast in Palm City took in all 36 dogs, including three puppies up to six months old. Sarah Fisher, a spokeswoman for the shelter, called it the worst case the organization has ever seen. Staff found rusted metal and glass shards stuck in the dogs' matted fur, and some dogs had bleeding tongues from biting themselves. One puppy had three pounds of mats removed during grooming.

The arrest followed an investigation that began in July after authorities received a letter and photographs from neighbors documenting concerns about the property. O'Donnell met with Animal Services at a Palm City park with one dog but would not allow investigators inside her home. An employee at a local animal hospital told investigators O'Donnell had brought in numerous puppies over the years and that records showed roughly 38 adult dogs had been treated there, including some brought in deceased. The arrest report says Animal Services had responded to roughly 20 incidents involving the residence from 2020 through this year.

The Humane Society said many of the dogs have skin and eye infections and appear withdrawn and catatonic. Some are being shaved under mild sedation due to emotional distress and physical pain. The shelter asked for monetary donations to its emergency medical fund to cover the cost of care. Fisher said the dogs will not be ready for adoption any time soon, but the shelter is running a name-your-own-price promotion to encourage adoptions of other animals and clear space.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County officials outline 2026 master plan for Port of Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Port officials discussed a master plan Tuesday that includes a mega-yacht marine facility and support hub for launch and rocket recovery operations at the Port of Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County officials discussed the 2026 master plan for the Port of Fort Pierce during an informal meeting in Fort Pierce Tuesday morning, aiming to clarify confusion about the plan's scope and details. The port, home to Derecktor Shipyards where mega-yacht maintenance and repairs take place, is set to see significant changes under the proposed plan. It includes a mega-yacht marine facility to expand the repair area and a support hub for launch and rocket recovery operations, which county officials believe aligns well with the port's existing capabilities.

The plan also proposes upgrades to the boat ramps at Harbour Pointe Park and the potential addition of an event center and fishing pier at Museum Pointe Park. Residents raised concerns about the history center located in Museum Pointe Park, which some fear could be removed to accommodate the project. County officials reassured attendees that the museum would remain in Fort Pierce.

Port officials plan to present the master plan to the City of Fort Pierce and the Town of St. Lucie Village to gather feedback and share it with the board. Joshua Revord, the county's director of port, inlet and beaches, said the plan could bring significant capital dollars and work volume to the area through maintenance, repair and overhaul of large vessels used in the industry.

cards.headline: Indian River County deputies talk wanted man off 17th Street Bridge after two-hour standoff
cards.teaser: Indian River County sheriff's deputies successfully ended a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach after talking a man wanted for burglary back from the edge. De
cards.body:
Indian River County sheriff's deputies successfully ended a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach after talking a man wanted for burglary back from the edge. Deputies were called to the bridge on Sunday, August 2, after receiving information that a man wanted on a Port St. Lucie Police Department warrant for burglary with battery had contacted his mother and made concerning statements.

Deputies located the man on top of the 17th Street Bridge after he climbed over the railing and threatened to jump. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office Crisis Negotiation Team spent about two hours talking with him while the Marine Unit launched a boat below the bridge. Fire Rescue also staged nearby as a safety precaution.

Body camera footage shows negotiators working to keep the man talking and convince him to come back over the railing. The man said he was worried about going to jail and the financial burden his family could face. Negotiators continued talking with him, eventually learning that he enjoyed playing video games. As the conversation continued, deputies told him his mother was heading to the base of the bridge.

The man eventually agreed to climb back over the railing. Body camera footage shows deputies encouraging him as he grabbed a ladder and climbed back onto the bridge. The man was then taken into custody without incident. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released the body camera footage along with information about the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, which can be reached by calling or texting 988.

cards.headline: Driver arrested for speeding through Fort Pierce school zone on first day of classes
cards.teaser: A 24-year-old man was arrested for driving 43 mph in a 20-mph school zone near Lawnwood Elementary School on the first day of school.
cards.body:
A driver was arrested for allegedly speeding through a school zone on the first day of school in Fort Pierce, according to police. The incident happened on Virginia Avenue near Lawnwood Elementary School.

Police said 24-year-old Miguel Angel Hernandez-Hernandez was driving 43 mph in a 20-mph school zone, more than double the posted speed limit. According to investigators, Hernandez-Hernandez was also driving without a valid license. He was arrested and booked into jail. No injuries were reported.

Police are reminding drivers to slow down and stay alert in school zones as students return to class for the new school year.

cards.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
cards.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

hero.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
hero.body:
Paige O'Donnell, 62, was arrested Monday after Martin County deputies executed a search warrant at her home on Alligator Street in Palm City and discovered 36 Border Collies living in severe neglect. O'Donnell faces 72 criminal charges: one felony animal torture charge and one misdemeanor confinement charge for each dog. Her bond was set at $270,000, and a judge ordered her not to possess any animals if released.

Deputies found the dogs covered in feces and urine inside a home where the air conditioning was not working and floors were covered in waste and garbage. Sheriff John Budensiek said some of the normally black-and-white Border Collies were so covered in feces they appeared nearly solid black. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast in Palm City took in all 36 dogs, including three puppies up to six months old. Sarah Fisher, a spokeswoman for the shelter, called it the worst case the organization has ever seen. Staff found rusted metal and glass shards stuck in the dogs' matted fur, and some dogs had bleeding tongues from biting themselves. One puppy had three pounds of mats removed during grooming.

The arrest followed an investigation that began in July after authorities received a letter and photographs from neighbors documenting concerns about the property. O'Donnell met with Animal Services at a Palm City park with one dog but would not allow investigators inside her home. An employee at a local animal hospital told investigators O'Donnell had brought in numerous puppies over the years and that records showed roughly 38 adult dogs had been treated there, including some brought in deceased. The arrest report says Animal Services had responded to roughly 20 incidents involving the residence from 2020 through this year.

The Humane Society said many of the dogs have skin and eye infections and appear withdrawn and catatonic. Some are being shaved under mild sedation due to emotional distress and physical pain. The shelter asked for monetary donations to its emergency medical fund to cover the cost of care. Fisher said the dogs will not be ready for adoption any time soon, but the shelter is running a name-your-own-price promotion to encourage adoptions of other animals and clear space.

hero.headline: Construction worker killed by vehicle in I-95 work zone south of Tradition
hero.teaser: A 45-year-old dump truck driver was killed after being hit by another construction vehicle inside a work zone on I-95 just south of Tradition on Monday night, according to the Flor
hero.body:
A 45-year-old dump truck driver was killed after being hit by another construction vehicle inside a work zone on I-95 just south of Tradition on Monday night, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The driver stepped out of their dump truck on the northbound lanes and was struck by a tractor with a sweeper traveling south, repaving the area as part of an improvement project.

The construction worker was transported to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, where they later died. The driver of the other truck was arrested on an unrelated warrant, FHP said.

The incident occurred during an improvement project on I-95 in Port St. Lucie. Workers were actively repaving the area when the fatal collision took place. The agency has not released the names of those involved in the crash.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County officials outline 2026 master plan for Port of Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Port officials discussed a master plan Tuesday that includes a mega-yacht marine facility and support hub for launch and rocket recovery operations at the Port of Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County officials discussed the 2026 master plan for the Port of Fort Pierce during an informal meeting in Fort Pierce Tuesday morning, aiming to clarify confusion about the plan's scope and details. The port, home to Derecktor Shipyards where mega-yacht maintenance and repairs take place, is set to see significant changes under the proposed plan. It includes a mega-yacht marine facility to expand the repair area and a support hub for launch and rocket recovery operations, which county officials believe aligns well with the port's existing capabilities.

The plan also proposes upgrades to the boat ramps at Harbour Pointe Park and the potential addition of an event center and fishing pier at Museum Pointe Park. Residents raised concerns about the history center located in Museum Pointe Park, which some fear could be removed to accommodate the project. County officials reassured attendees that the museum would remain in Fort Pierce.

Port officials plan to present the master plan to the City of Fort Pierce and the Town of St. Lucie Village to gather feedback and share it with the board. Joshua Revord, the county's director of port, inlet and beaches, said the plan could bring significant capital dollars and work volume to the area through maintenance, repair and overhaul of large vessels used in the industry.

cards.headline: Driver arrested for speeding through Fort Pierce school zone on first day of classes
cards.teaser: A 24-year-old man was arrested for driving 43 mph in a 20-mph school zone near Lawnwood Elementary School on the first day of school.
cards.body:
A driver was arrested for allegedly speeding through a school zone on the first day of school in Fort Pierce, according to police. The incident happened on Virginia Avenue near Lawnwood Elementary School.

Police said 24-year-old Miguel Angel Hernandez-Hernandez was driving 43 mph in a 20-mph school zone, more than double the posted speed limit. According to investigators, Hernandez-Hernandez was also driving without a valid license. He was arrested and booked into jail. No injuries were reported.

Police are reminding drivers to slow down and stay alert in school zones as students return to class for the new school year.

hero.headline: Indian River County deputies talk wanted man off 17th Street Bridge after two-hour standoff
hero.teaser: Indian River County sheriff's deputies successfully ended a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach after talking a man wanted for burglary back from the edge. De
hero.body:
Indian River County sheriff's deputies successfully ended a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge in Vero Beach after talking a man wanted for burglary back from the edge. Deputies were called to the bridge on Sunday, August 2, after receiving information that a man wanted on a Port St. Lucie Police Department warrant for burglary with battery had contacted his mother and made concerning statements.

Deputies located the man on top of the 17th Street Bridge after he climbed over the railing and threatened to jump. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office Crisis Negotiation Team spent about two hours talking with him while the Marine Unit launched a boat below the bridge. Fire Rescue also staged nearby as a safety precaution.

Body camera footage shows negotiators working to keep the man talking and convince him to come back over the railing. The man said he was worried about going to jail and the financial burden his family could face. Negotiators continued talking with him, eventually learning that he enjoyed playing video games. As the conversation continued, deputies told him his mother was heading to the base of the bridge.

The man eventually agreed to climb back over the railing. Body camera footage shows deputies encouraging him as he grabbed a ladder and climbed back onto the bridge. The man was then taken into custody without incident. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released the body camera footage along with information about the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, which can be reached by calling or texting 988.
